title: Blue Jacaranda: Ancient Jacarandas You Can Visit
meta_description: A South American tree that turns entire crowns violet-blue each spring, mapped from a Cagliari park to a walled Cordoba garden shut for four centuries.
intro: For a few weeks a year a jacaranda stops looking like any other tree, its whole crown turning violet-blue and the ground beneath carpeting in the same colour when the flowers drop, which is why cities from Pretoria to Sydney planted it far outside its native Argentina and Bolivia. Cagliari's specimen in the Giardini Pubblici does this every May among trees chosen for shade rather than spectacle. Cordoba's grew inside a walled garden that belonged first to a Dominican convent and then to a Renaissance palace, invisible from the street until the gate finally opened to the public in 2004. Sydney's is the odd one out: the jacaranda that made the University of Sydney's Quadrangle famous fell in 2016 after 88 years, and the tree standing there now is a clone planted the following year, carrying the same genetics and almost none of the age.
